stories.title: Tether pushes its gold-backed token as an ETF rival
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports Tether wants its gold-backed token to compete with gold ETFs. The report frames this as part of Tether's push beyond stablecoins into tokenized commodities. It does not give details on the token's backing structure or regulatory status.
stories.whyItMatters: Tether is the largest stablecoin issuer. Its move into gold tokens could change how investors get gold exposure on-chain.
whatToWatch: Watch for adoption or trading volume data on the token.
Watch for regulatory comment, given Tether's past scrutiny.
questions: How does the token's backing and redemption process compare to a gold ETF?
What regulatory framework, if any, covers this token?

sources.title: Tether wants its gold token to rival ETFs

stories.title: A stablecoin holding would have gained from currency moves, not interest
stories.summary: CryptoSlate describes a case where $10,000 held in stablecoins would have gained about €420, driven by currency exchange moves rather than interest. The report frames this as a reminder that stablecoin returns can come from FX swings, not yield.
stories.whyItMatters: Readers who use stablecoins for dollar exposure should know the source of any gain. FX-driven gains work differently from yield products and carry different risks.
whatToWatch: Further currency moves that could add to or erase this gain.
Any regulatory comment on how non-yield stablecoin gains are presented.
questions: Which stablecoin and time period does this calculation use?
Does this reflect a broader dollar trend or a one-off move?

sources.title: How $10,000 in stablecoins would have gained €420 without earning interest

stories.title: Bitcoin looks cheap by one measure after $1 billion in ETF outflows
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports about $1 billion left Bitcoin ETFs recently. Despite this, the report says bitcoin now looks cheap by at least one valuation measure. The article does not name the specific measure or the time frame for the outflows.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are a key read on institutional sentiment. Large outflows next to a cheap valuation signal is a split readers should watch closely.
whatToWatch: Whether ETF outflows continue or reverse in coming flow reports.
Whether bitcoin's price responds to the cheap valuation signal.
questions: Which valuation measure is being cited?
Over what period did the $1 billion in outflows occur?

sources.title: Bitcoin now looks cheap by one measure after $1 billion in ETF outflows

stories.title: Ethereum called 'worst asset of all time' amid BitMine's estimated $8.83B loss
stories.summary: CryptoSlate raises the question of whether Ethereum is the "worst asset of all time," tied to an estimated $8.83 billion loss at BitMine. The framing points to scrutiny of corporate ETH treasury strategies. The report does not detail how the loss figure was calculated.
stories.whyItMatters: Corporate ETH treasury bets have grown as a strategy. A loss this large raises questions about that approach and about ETH's price path.
whatToWatch: BitMine's next disclosures on its ETH holdings and losses.
Further market commentary on ETH's performance.
questions: How was the $8.83 billion loss figure estimated, and over what period?
What is BitMine's current ETH position?

sources.title: Is Ethereum the “worst asset of all time,” amid estimated $8.83 billion BitMine loss ?

stories.title: Britain plans £4B grid fix — could Bitcoin miners use the wasted wind power?
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports the UK plans to spend £4 billion to fix electricity grid bottlenecks. The article asks whether curtailed wind power, currently going unused, could instead power Bitcoin mining. It gives no detail on any actual proposal or government position on this.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin mining's energy use is a recurring policy issue. Linking it to grid planning ties the industry's footprint to national energy policy.
whatToWatch: Any formal UK proposal linking curtailed wind power to crypto mining.
Progress on the £4 billion grid spending plan.
questions: Is there an actual proposal under discussion, or is this a speculative idea?
Would UK regulators allow mining to use curtailed power this way?

sources.title: Britain to spend £4 billion on grid bottlenecks. Can Bitcoin use the wasted wind?

stories.title: A Fed rescue of bond markets could still hurt Bitcoin, analysts say
stories.summary: CryptoSlate covers analysis arguing the Federal Reserve could act to support bond markets in a way that still works against Bitcoin. The report does not specify the exact policy mechanism or timeline involved.
stories.whyItMatters: Fed policy and liquidity conditions drive bitcoin's price. A path that helps bonds but hurts BTC marks a divergence worth tracking.
whatToWatch: Upcoming Fed decisions and statements on bond market support.
Bitcoin's price reaction to any Fed action.
questions: What specific Fed mechanism is under discussion?
What is the transmission channel from Fed bond support to Bitcoin weakness?

sources.title: The Fed could rescue bond markets and still make life harder for Bitcoin

stories.title: Robots run AI-written code without AI oversight, with a 92% success rate
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that robots executed AI-generated code without an AI directing the execution, and reached a 92% success rate in testing. The report does not name the research group, test setup, or task types used.
stories.whyItMatters: This story sits outside core crypto markets, but autonomous AI-and-robot pipelines could feed into on-chain automation and agentic crypto tools that readers follow.
whatToWatch: More detail on the research behind the 92% figure.
Any link between this work and crypto-related AI agent projects.
questions: Which organization ran this test, and on what tasks?
Is there a direct crypto angle, or is this general robotics research?

sources.title: Robots now run AI-written code without an AI calling the shots, succeeding 92% of the time

stories.title: Lido's lending plan may block loan repayments while interest still accrues
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports a design issue in Lido's lending plan: borrowers could find themselves blocked from repaying loans, even as interest keeps accruing. The report does not say whether this has been exploited or affected any funds so far.
stories.whyItMatters: Lido is the largest liquid-staking protocol. A flaw in an adjacent lending feature carries outsized risk for ETH stakers and DeFi users who rely on it.
whatToWatch: Whether Lido issues a fix or public statement.
Whether any user funds have been affected.
questions: Is this a theoretical risk, or has it already affected users?
What is Lido's timeline for addressing the issue?

stories.title: AI models agreed with each other more than with reality, test finds
stories.summary: CryptoSlate covers a test finding that AI models agreed with each other more often than they matched ground truth. The report does not name the models tested or describe the test's methodology.
stories.whyItMatters: Readers who use AI tools to analyze crypto markets or on-chain data should note that model agreement does not guarantee accuracy.
whatToWatch: More detail on which models and benchmark were used.
Whether this finding applies to AI tools used for crypto-specific analysis.
questions: Which AI models and benchmark were tested?
Does the finding extend to crypto market analysis tools specifically?

stories.title: AI helped hackers breach 10 unnamed organizations, researchers say
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that researchers found AI tools helped attackers gain access at 10 organizations. The organizations were not named, and the report gives no detail on their sectors or the exact methods used.
stories.whyItMatters: Crypto exchanges and protocols are frequent targets of sophisticated attacks, so AI-assisted hacking methods are directly relevant to the industry's security.
whatToWatch: Whether researchers name the affected organizations or sectors.
Whether any crypto exchanges or protocols are confirmed among the victims.
questions: Were any crypto exchanges or protocols among the 10 organizations?
What specific AI techniques aided these breaches?
